sets.title: Law and method changes
sets.what: Changes since 2016 that break year-to-year comparisons.
rows: HF 516 cut the absentee/early window from 40 to 29 days (Iowa Code 53.10, 53.11, 53.8); also voter ID (soft in 2018, required from 1/1/2019) and ended straight-party voting
2016 accumulates from 9/29 (40 days); 2018 and 2020 from 29 days out. Same days-before-ED is not the same days of voting.

SF 413 cut the window from 29 to 20 days; mail ballots must now be RECEIVED by poll close on ED (the postmark-by-day-before rule was struck); at most one drop box per county, at the auditor's office; polls close 8 p.m. (was 9 p.m.); voters marked inactive after missing a general

2016-2020 lines start 9-20 days earlier than 2022-2026: at E-11 2018 had about 18 days of voting, 2026 about 9. Late-arriving mail counted in 2016-2020 is not counted from 2022. Compare 2026 with 2022 and 2024 first.
Iowa Code 2026 s.53.10 and 53.17 (as printed 12/2025): in-person absentee from 20 days before ED; return envelope received no later than poll close; one drop box per commissioner
Confirms the 2022-2026 regime is unchanged for 2026.

HF 954 (2025): absentee counting board convenes no later than 9 a.m. on ED and must allow time to finish all absentee ballots by 10 p.m.; DOT noncitizen files used in list checks; ranked-choice voting barred (Division II, eff. 1/1/2026)
Absentee results still reported on election night; no pre-ED tabulation except the s.53.23 exception (board may start the day before if the previous general's count ran past 10 p.m.).
IA-01..04 and State House/Senate lines are the same in 2022, 2024 and 2026: district comparisons 2022-2026 are like for like; 2016-2020 are not.
late-arriving mail counted (or not): final mail counts and post-ED count timing differ
